title: clusters/manifest.json
description: Stage 1 output. Index of the segmented corpus. One entry per cluster — a coherent unit that can carry independent evidence. The projectibility probe requires a regularity to appear in at least two independent clusters, so cluster identity is load-bearing, not cosmetic.

id.description: Stable cluster id, e.g. 'c01'. Referenced by extractions.json.

source.description: Path to the extracted plain text this cluster came from, relative to the work dir, e.g. 'raw/book.txt'.

kind.description: Drives auto-weighting in Stage 3. Dialogue and decision_record tokens both count toward dialogue_ratio in the coverage map.

period.description: Year or span the cluster belongs to, e.g. '2018' or '2011-2014'. Omit when undatable.

tokens.description: Approximate token count. A two-sentence cluster corroborates nothing — keep each large enough to be meaningful.

attribution.description: Whose words these are. firsthand = the person's own (book, essay, transcript turns, posts, their commit messages); secondhand = someone writing about them (summaries, study notes, paraphrase, analysis); mixed = quotation embedded in another author's commentary; unknown = authorship undeterminable. Required, because three hard rules depend on it: expression and modulation extraction runs on firsthand clusters only, a projectible regularity needs at least one firsthand cluster, and cost-refusals or interactional moves sourced only from secondhand material are flagged unverified and cannot satisfy the Stage 5 presence assertion. See acquisition.md.

source_url.description: Where this cluster came from, when the source is remote — repository, page, or file URL. Keep it even after grouping short wiki pages into one cluster, so provenance survives the merge. Omit for local corpora.

retrieved.description: ISO 8601 date of retrieval. Remote content changes under you; without this a re-run is not the same run.

revision.description: Commit SHA for git sources. The reproducibility anchor a URL alone cannot give you.
